title: Open-Source Weight Release + Governance Vacuum: Measuring the Uncontrolled Capability Diffusion Risk

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: quantifying the fraction of high-capability open-weight releases with no governance makes the open-weight governance problem concrete and motivates policy action.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: identifying open-weight releases and coding their release governance from public information is accessible. Capability thresholds can be defined using existing benchmarks.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: identify releases above threshold, code governance for each against checklist, compute fraction. Well-bounded methodology.

novelty.reasoning: This is substantially addressed by recent research and policy work. OECD.AI published 'AI Openness: Balancing Innovation, Transparency and Risk in Open-Weight Models' (2025). UK AISI published 'Managing Risks from Increasingly Capable Open-Weight AI Systems' (2025). 'Open Technical Problems in Open-Weight AI Model Risk Management' (SSRN, 2025) systematically catalogues governance gaps. 'State of Open-Source AI 2025' tracks the landscape. The Centre for Future Generations published 'Can Open-Weight Models Ever Be Safe?' and 'Beyond the Binary' (2025). The specific measurement—fraction of high-capability open-weight releases with no governance—is essentially what these reports already quantify. Epoch AI data on the closing capability gap (5-22 months lag) is published. The contribution is largely subsumed.
